children: The supply of soymeal--soybeans ground for use in numerous products, including food or processing into soybean oil--appears to be tight as users of soymeal struggle to buy supply. Basis levels, or the difference between the local cash price of soybeans and the price of the nearest futures contract on an exchange like the CBOT, around the Midwest are strengthening, says Brian Hoops of Midwest Market Solutions. "Rainfall is slowing harvest and limiting the amount of product that is flowing to the processors," he adds. Basis levels for soybeans around the country are generally higher than seen at this time last year, with many buyers willing to pay extra on top of where soybeans are trading at on the CBOT. Most-active soybean futures are up 0.2%, to nearly $13.40 a bushel. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
